_comment: 500-entry dataset of atomic technical/causal claims extracted primarily from well-known ML/AI research papers. Lighter schema than the physics propositions.json (no formal context/MONOTONIC_* apparatus) -- this is a paper-claim extraction dataset, not a formal K-IR benchmark, though the same 'one atomic idea per entry, cite the source' discipline applies. Building in batches; see README.md for progress and schema.

entries.paper: Vaswani et al. 2017 (Attention Is All You Need)
entries.claim: The Transformer architecture replaces recurrence entirely with self-attention for sequence modeling.
Scaled dot-product attention divides QK^T by sqrt(d_k) before softmax, preventing large-magnitude dot products from pushing softmax into low-gradient saturation regions.
Multi-head attention runs several attention operations in parallel on different learned linear projections of Q/K/V, letting the model attend to different representation subspaces simultaneously.
Sinusoidal positional encodings inject sequence-order information into token embeddings because self-attention itself is permutation-invariant.
Self-attention computes pairwise interactions between all token pairs, costing O(n^2) time and memory in sequence length n.
Residual connections around each Transformer sub-layer, combined with layer normalization, stabilize training of deep Transformer stacks.
The Transformer decoder uses masked self-attention so a position cannot attend to future positions during autoregressive generation.
Cross-attention in encoder-decoder Transformers lets decoder queries attend to encoder key/value pairs, connecting source and target sequences.
BERT uses a bidirectional Transformer encoder pretrained with masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction.
GPT uses a unidirectional (causal) Transformer decoder pretrained by next-token prediction.
Scaling a causal Transformer language model up in parameters and training data improves its zero-shot task performance.
A sufficiently large autoregressive language model can perform few-shot learning from examples placed in the prompt, without any gradient updates.
T5 reframes every NLP task as text-to-text and trains a single encoder-decoder Transformer on this unified format.
The Vision Transformer applies a standard Transformer encoder to a sequence of image patches instead of using convolutions.
FlashAttention reduces the memory and wall-clock cost of exact attention by fusing operations and avoiding materializing the full attention matrix in slow GPU memory.
Rotary position embeddings encode relative position information by rotating query and key vectors as a function of token position.
Relative position representations let attention scores depend on the relative distance between tokens rather than only absolute position.
Sparse attention patterns restrict each token to attend to a limited set of positions, reducing the quadratic cost of full self-attention for long sequences.
Layer normalization is the standard normalization used inside Transformer blocks because, unlike batch normalization, it does not depend on batch statistics.
Applying layer normalization before each sub-layer (Pre-LN), rather than after (Post-LN), trains more stably at greater Transformer depth.
Stochastic Gradient Descent updates parameters using the gradient estimated from a small random mini-batch rather than the full dataset, trading gradient accuracy for computational efficiency.
Momentum accumulates an exponentially decaying moving average of past gradients to accelerate convergence and dampen oscillation in narrow loss-surface valleys.
Nesterov accelerated gradient evaluates the gradient at a momentum-adjusted look-ahead point rather than the current position, improving convergence over classical momentum.
AdaGrad adapts each parameter's learning rate by dividing by the square root of the sum of its past squared gradients, giving infrequently-updated parameters larger effective steps.
AdaGrad's accumulated squared-gradient denominator grows monotonically, causing its effective learning rate to shrink toward zero over long training runs.
RMSProp fixes AdaGrad's vanishing-learning-rate problem by using an exponentially decaying moving average of squared gradients instead of a cumulative sum.
Adam combines a momentum-style first moment estimate with an RMSProp-style adaptive second moment estimate, plus bias correction for both.
Adam's bias-correction terms compensate for its moment estimates being initialized at zero, which would otherwise bias early-training updates toward zero.
AdamW decouples weight decay from the gradient-based update, applying it directly to the weights instead of folding it into the gradient as plain Adam with L2 regularization does.

entries.paper: Common practice; e.g. Vaswani et al. 2017
entries.claim: Learning-rate warmup gradually increases the learning rate from a small value at training start, stabilizing early training of large models like Transformers.
Cosine learning-rate decay anneals the learning rate along a cosine curve toward a minimum over training, often combined with periodic warm restarts.
Gradient clipping caps the norm of gradients before the parameter update, preventing exploding gradients from destabilizing training, especially in RNNs.
LAMB extends Adam-style updates with per-layer adaptive learning-rate scaling based on the ratio of weight norm to update norm, enabling stable large-batch training.
Linear learning-rate scaling with batch size preserves training dynamics when using large-batch data-parallel training.

Second-order optimization methods use curvature information (an approximation to the Hessian or Fisher information matrix) to precondition gradient updates, at higher per-step compute cost than first-order methods.
Adam's default hyperparameters beta1=0.9 and beta2=0.999 set the decay rates of its first and second moment moving averages respectively.
Weight decay penalizes the squared norm of the weights, encouraging smaller weights and acting as a form of L2 regularization.
A learning-rate decay phase is used because a constant rate large enough for fast early progress is typically too large to allow convergence to a sharp minimum late in training.
Lookahead maintains slow-moving anchor weights that periodically pull toward fast weights updated by an inner optimizer, improving training stability.
Sharpness-Aware Minimization seeks parameters in flat regions of the loss landscape by minimizing the worst-case loss within a neighborhood of current weights, improving generalization.
Dropout randomly zeroes a fraction of unit activations during training, preventing co-adaptation of neurons and acting as an implicit ensemble of subnetworks.
At test time, dropout is disabled, with activations scaled (inverted dropout) to match the expected magnitude seen during training.
Batch normalization normalizes layer activations using the mean and variance computed over each mini-batch, then applies a learned scale and shift.
Batch normalization's main empirical benefit is smoothing the optimization landscape, not reducing internal covariate shift as originally proposed by Ioffe & Szegedy.
Batch normalization's statistics depend on batch composition, making it less effective with very small batch sizes or online/streaming training.
Layer normalization normalizes across the feature dimension for each example rather than across the batch, making it independent of batch size.
Weight decay (L2 regularization) biases the optimizer toward simpler models with smaller parameter values.
Early stopping halts training when validation loss stops improving, preventing the model from continuing to fit noise in the training data after the point of best generalization.
Label smoothing replaces hard one-hot classification targets with a mixture of the one-hot target and a uniform distribution, discouraging over-confident predictions.
Data augmentation artificially expands the effective training set via label-preserving transformations, improving generalization.
Mixup trains on convex combinations of pairs of training examples and their labels, encouraging the model to behave linearly between training examples.

Stochastic depth randomly drops entire residual layers during training while keeping the identity shortcut, reducing effective network depth per step and improving generalization in very deep ResNets.
DropConnect generalizes dropout by randomly zeroing individual weights (connections) rather than whole unit activations.
Cutout regularizes CNN training for images by masking out random contiguous square regions of the input during training.
Spectral normalization constrains the largest singular value of each weight matrix, stabilizing GAN discriminator training by enforcing an approximate Lipschitz constraint.
WGAN-GP's gradient penalty term penalizes deviation of the discriminator's gradient norm from 1, enforcing an approximate Lipschitz constraint without weight clipping.
Ensembling multiple independently trained models and averaging their predictions typically improves generalization over any single model, at extra training and inference cost.
Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student model to match the softened output distribution of a larger teacher model, rather than only hard labels.

Batch normalization's learned scale and shift parameters let the network recover the original unnormalized representation if that is optimal, so normalization does not reduce representational capacity.
Elastic Weight Consolidation regularizes continual learning by penalizing changes to parameters that were important for previously learned tasks, mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
LeNet-5 combines convolution, subsampling (pooling), and fully connected layers for handwritten digit recognition, an early convolutional architecture.
AlexNet showed that a deep CNN trained on GPUs with ReLU activations and dropout dramatically outperformed prior methods on ImageNet classification.
ReLU activations avoid the vanishing-gradient problem of saturating activations like sigmoid/tanh for positive inputs, a key factor in AlexNet's success.
Stacking many small 3x3 convolution filters achieves a larger effective receptive field with fewer parameters than fewer large filters, while adding non-linearity between them.
Inception modules apply multiple filter sizes (1x1, 3x3, 5x5) in parallel within the same layer and concatenate their outputs.
1x1 convolutions in Inception modules reduce channel dimensionality as a bottleneck before more expensive larger convolutions, cutting computational cost.
ResNet's residual (skip) connections let a layer learn a residual function relative to its input, mitigating vanishing gradients and enabling training of networks over 100 layers deep.
Before ResNet, simply stacking more layers in plain CNNs was empirically observed to increase training error, the 'degradation problem' that residual connections address.
DenseNet connects each layer to every other layer in a feed-forward fashion within a block, encouraging feature reuse and alleviating vanishing gradients.
Batch normalization is commonly placed after convolution and before the non-linearity in CNN blocks, stabilizing and accelerating training.

entries.paper: He et al. 2015 (ResNet); Lin et al. 2013 (NiN)
entries.claim: Global average pooling reduces each feature map to a single value by averaging, cutting parameter count and reducing overfitting compared to flattening plus dense layers.
MobileNet uses depthwise separable convolutions -- a depthwise spatial convolution followed by a pointwise 1x1 convolution -- to reduce computation for mobile/embedded deployment.
EfficientNet's compound scaling method jointly scales network depth, width, and input resolution according to a fixed ratio found via neural architecture search.
U-Net's encoder-decoder CNN uses skip connections between corresponding encoder and decoder layers, preserving fine spatial detail for pixel-level tasks like segmentation.
Faster R-CNN's Region Proposal Network shares convolutional features with the detection head, making object proposal generation nearly cost-free compared to earlier two-stage detectors.
YOLO reframes object detection as a single regression problem, directly predicting bounding boxes and class probabilities from a full image in one forward pass, trading some accuracy for speed.
Mask R-CNN extends Faster R-CNN by adding a parallel branch that predicts a segmentation mask for each detected object, alongside classification and box regression.
Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks adaptively reweight channel-wise feature responses using a learned per-channel gating mechanism, improving representational power at low extra cost.
Dilated (atrous) convolutions increase a convolution's receptive field without increasing parameter count or reducing spatial resolution, by inserting gaps between kernel elements.
CNNs pretrained on large datasets like ImageNet and fine-tuned on a smaller target dataset typically outperform training from random initialization when target data is limited.
Recurrent Neural Networks process sequences by maintaining a hidden state updated at each time step as a function of the current input and the previous hidden state.

entries.paper: Bengio et al. 1994; Pascanu et al. 2013
entries.claim: Vanilla RNNs suffer from vanishing and exploding gradients over long sequences because gradients are repeatedly multiplied by the same recurrent weight matrix during backpropagation through time.
The LSTM's memory cell with input, forget, and output gates lets gradients flow through many time steps largely unattenuated, mitigating vanishing gradients.
The LSTM forget gate learns to decide how much of the previous cell state to retain versus discard at each time step.
The Gated Recurrent Unit simplifies the LSTM by merging the cell and hidden state and using two gates (reset and update) instead of three, with fewer parameters.
Sequence-to-sequence models use an encoder RNN to compress an input sequence into a fixed-size vector and a decoder RNN to generate an output sequence from that vector.
A fixed-size context vector in vanilla seq2seq models creates an information bottleneck that degrades performance on long input sequences, motivating attention mechanisms.
Bahdanau attention lets the decoder at each output step compute a weighted combination of all encoder hidden states, rather than relying on a single fixed context vector.
Luong attention introduced simpler global and local attention scoring functions, such as dot-product, as alternatives to Bahdanau's additive attention.
Bidirectional RNNs process a sequence in both forward and backward directions and combine the resulting hidden states, giving each position access to both past and future context.

Teacher forcing trains sequence generation models by feeding the ground-truth previous token as input at each decoding step, speeding up training but causing train/inference mismatch known as exposure bias.
Beam search decoding keeps the top-k highest-scoring partial sequences at each generation step, exploring more of the output space than greedy decoding at added computational cost.
Truncated backpropagation through time limits gradient computation to a fixed number of past time steps, trading exact gradients for tractable memory and compute on long sequences.
ELMo produces contextualized word representations from the internal states of a bidirectional LSTM language model, so a word's embedding depends on its surrounding context.
Connectionist Temporal Classification allows training sequence models, such as for speech recognition, without requiring exact frame-level alignment between input and output sequences.
Peephole connections let LSTM gates observe the cell state directly, rather than only the previous hidden state, improving modeling of precise timing.
Stacked multi-layer RNNs pass the hidden-state sequence of one recurrent layer as input to the next, letting the model learn hierarchical temporal representations.
RNN-based language models estimate the probability of a token conditioned on all previous tokens by recursively updating a hidden state, factorizing sequence probability via the chain rule.
Gradient clipping is especially important when training RNNs because exploding gradients are common from repeated multiplication through the recurrent weight matrix over many time steps.
Attention mechanisms originally developed for RNN-based seq2seq models were later shown to be sufficient on their own, without recurrence, giving rise to the Transformer.
